candidates.exact_span: Regulations contained in 40 CFR §122.44 requires that NPDES permit limits are developed that meet the more stringent of either technology-based effluent limitation guidelines, numerical and/or narrative water quality standard-based effluent limits, or the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of the more-stringent-of rule could change which numeric or narrative limit is selected as the applicable enforceable limit for a given parameter and monitoring period.

candidates.exact_span: Regulations found in 40 CFR 411.13 and 411.17 define BAT and BCT effluent limitations, respectively, for cement manufacturing non-leaching process, and 40 CFR 411.37 defines BCT effluent guidelines for materials storage piles runoff from cement manufacturing facilities.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which ELG subparts govern this facility's discharge type determines which technology-based numeric limits are candidates for applicability at evaluated outfalls.

candidates.exact_span: Effluent limitations established at Outfall 001 in the current permit regulate overflows from Quarry #1 pond which stores storm runoff and process water effluent from plant areas.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of which discharge points and flows are covered by Outfall 001 limits affects which parameters and outfalls receive enforceable limits (A) and which discharge-driven monitoring obligations attach to those flows (B).

candidates.exact_span: The 40 CFR 411.37 ELG of 50 mg/l was the basis for establishment of TSS effluent limitation at Outfall 001.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage ties the operative TSS numeric limit at Outfall 001 to a specific ELG value; a different reading of basis versus actual permit language could change the enforceable limit used in exceedance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: EPA did not establish 40 CFR 411.13 temperature limitation at Outfall 001 because discharges at Outfall 001 would be intermittent and the permit restricted discharges due to catastrophic or chronic precipitation events.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether temperature is subject to an enforceable numeric limit (A), whether monitoring for temperature is required only under certain discharge or precipitation conditions (B), and how intermittent or restricted-discharge periods are classified for missing or conditional evidence (C) all depend on how these discharge restrictions and non-establishment rationale are interpreted.

candidates.exact_span: The 40 CFR 411.17 TSS mass load limitation might not be applicable at Outfall 001 because the combination of storm runoff and process water.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The stated uncertainty about mass-load applicability could change whether a mass-based TSS limit is enforceable (A) and whether mass-load monitoring or reporting is required versus report-only or not applicable (B).

candidates.exact_span: TSS reported maximum daily discharge did exceed the daily max limit of 50 mg/l.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This documents a prior exceedance against a daily maximum of 50 mg/l; interpretation of its evidentiary weight could affect whether the daily max remains the operative comparison basis or supports shifting to a different limit form.

candidates.exact_span: As a result, it is proposed in the draft permit that the permittee report 30-day average for TSS.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A proposed switch from daily maximum to 30-day average reporting could change the applicable numeric limit basis and exceedance metric (A) and alter the monitoring or reporting obligation for TSS (B).

candidates.exact_span: Water quality-based requirements are necessary where effluent limits more stringent than technology-based limits are necessary to maintain or achieve federal or state water quality limits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different interpretations of when WQBELs supersede technology-based limits could change which numeric or narrative limits are selected as the applicable enforceable limit.
